text.p: The groom wore midnight blue and the bride wore pearl-coloured silk at a wedding that was typical in every respect but one: the groom was John F. Kennedy Jr., a president's son who grew up to become America's most eligible bachelor.

Appropriately enough for the scion of a U.S. political dynasty, details of Saturday's hush-hush wedding of Kennedy, 35, and Carolyn Bessette, 29, on a remote island off the Georgia coast were released in Washington on Monday by the groom's uncle, Sen. Edward Kennedy of Massachusetts.

"This is a time of special joy for all of us in the Kennedy family," the senior Kennedy said in a statement. "I know that Jack and Jackie would be very proud of them and full of love for them as they began their future together."

He referred to President John F. Kennedy, assassinated in 1963, and Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, the society beauty whose every move and outfit were chronicled by the world's media until her death in 1994.
Fascination with the family is such that an auction of their possessions -- from golf clubs to costume jewelry -- in New York earlier this year brought unprecedented prices and attention.

So the marriage of John Jr., remembered by many as the toddler who saluted his assassinated father's coffin and was once proclaimed "the sexiest man alive" by People magazine, took on added significance.

The details were traditional: the bride, until recently an executive at Calvin Klein Industries, wore a long dress of pearl-coloured, bias-cut silk crepe, a veil of silk tulle and crystal-beaded silk satin sandals.
The groom wore a single-breasted midnight blue wool suit with a white pique vest and pale blue silk tie.
Caroline Kennedy Schlossberg, the groom's sister, was the matron of honour, with her daughters Rose and Tatiana serving as flower girls and her son Jack as ring bearer.
The best man was the groom's cousin, Anthony Radziwill, son of his maternal aunt Lee Radziwill and the late Prince Stanislas Radziwill.

Passages from scripture were read by the groom's brother-in-law, Edwin Schlossberg; the bride's sister, Lisa Bessette; the bride's brother-in-law, Michael Roman; the groom's cousin, Dr. William Kennedy Smith -- known to Kennedy-watchers as the acquitted defendant in a 1991 date-rape trial -- and Senator Kennedy.
The bride carried a bouquet of lily of the valley and the groom, best man and ring bearer wore boutonnieres of cornflowers, President Kennedy's favourite flower.
The couple cut a traditional three-tier wedding cake with vanilla buttercream frosting, decorated with flowers.
The media was effectively screened from the proceedings at a small chapel on Cumberland Island, a barrier island 18 1/2 miles (29 km) off the Georgia Coast.

The statement from Senator Kennedy's office said the couple had often visited the island, which had been owned by the family of the couple's close friend, Gogo Ferguson, until it was donated to the U.S. government as a national park.
Ferguson, who still lives on the island, designed the couple's wedding rings and is president of the Plum Orchard Centre for the Arts, on whose board the groom serves.

These sedate details seem at variance with media reports of the couple's recent past, including a screaming confrontation in New York's Central Park earlier this year which was videotaped and photographed.

Kennedy, who publishes the political magazine "George," had been living with Bessette for a year at the time. Before that, he had a widely publicised, on-and-off relationship with Hollywood star Darryl Hannah.
During the 1980s, after graduating from New York University law school, he worked briefly in the Manhattan District Attorney's office.
The couple plans to live in New York.
